newsitem.title: USA: Faulding unit cleared to market a generic.
newsitem.headline: Faulding unit cleared to market a generic.

text.p: Faulding Inc's Purepec Pharmaceutical Co has received the approval of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to sell pentoxifylline extended-release tablets.
The product is the generic equivalent of Hoechst Marion Roussel, Inc's Trental, used to treat chronic occlusive arterial disease of the limbs, Faulding said in a statement issued Wednesday.
Hoechst Marion, a unit of Germany's Hoechst AG, reported $172 million in Trental sales last year.
Other generic drug companies were also approved to make and market pentoxifylline, which had been off market since April 1997.
Faulding said it would begin commercial shipments of the product immediately.
Chronic occlusive arterial disease occurs when arteries in the limbs are clogged, a Faulding spokesman said. The tablets thin blood so it can more easily pass through the arteries.
